summary: Cattaraugus County 82.5-foot tower built by CCC men in 1940; closed in 1989 and removed in 1993, with a county communications tower built on the site.

facts.design: International Derrick model 1937 steel lookout tower, 82 ft 6 in
facts.status_note: Lookout removed in 1993; a county free-standing communications tower was built on the site. No source describes that tower's condition today.

staffing.status: lookout work ended after the 1988 season

facts.agency: New York State Conservation Department, built with Civilian Conservation Corps Camp 106 men

events.note: Ground broken in May 1940 by Hungry Hollow CCC camp workers; steel tower completed as an 82.5-foot lookout
Tower began hosting repeater antennas for the Cattaraugus County Sheriff's Office (per Wikipedia)
Fire lookout operations ceased at the end of the 1988 season
NYSDEC officially closed the tower in early 1989
Tower dismantled and removed as the county built a free-standing communications tower on the site

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia says the tower was first intended for Irish Hill, about six miles northeast of McCarty Hill; Starr's list says McCarty Hill is locally known as Irish Hill. The story uses McCarty Hill and reports both.
The 2022 newsletter says a smaller tower was no longer staffed after the war. That remark concerns the older Salamanca tower, not McCarty Hill, so it is not used for McCarty.

notes_for_editor: The 2022 newsletter's staffing remark ('no longer staffed') refers to the older Salamanca tower, not McCarty Hill; it is not used for McCarty. Name conflict: Irish Hill (see resolved_conflicts). Staffing (1941), repeater history (1987), closure (1989) and removal (1993) come from Wikipedia only; its reference list was not read in full. Starr's list marks the tower as removed. The 1940 build is supported by a 1940 newspaper extract and the 2022 newsletter. No source describes the 1993 communications tower's condition today, and no source says whether the summit is open to the public, so no access fact is recorded. The Salamanca Fire Tower is a different structure and is mentioned only to prevent confusion.
